hypothesis: The Official-only parent misses the pretraining gate because its token budget is far below the compute-optimal point, not because its data mix lacks a domain. Holding data identity, architecture, seed and schedule shape fixed and only raising the step budget improves the failing domain losses and reduces greedy-decoding repetition.

evidence: parent eval loss fell 2.4797 -> 2.3837 over its final 1,000 steps with no plateau
parent saw 122,880,000 tokens for 89,864,448 parameters, i.e. 1.37 tokens per parameter
three 1,000-step continuation pilots on new data mixes regressed every gate metric
the legacy archive holds 196 runs of 700-1,200 step anneals at learning rate 3e-7 to 8e-7 that moved test loss by about 0.001
rejected: data coverage: the same corpus that trained the threshold reference model is already in use
tokenizer: unchanged between parent and threshold reference
evaluation mismatch: strict holdout and MCQ already pass, only domain loss and repetition fail

arm.note: Only max_steps and the epoch allowance differ from the frozen parent recipe. The Official view holds about 844,000 packed blocks, so 60,000 steps at batch 32 is about 2.27 passes and needs an epoch allowance of 3.

stop_conditions: free disk below the training space budget
strict mean fails to improve by 0.02 over the parent, which would falsify the budget hypothesis
